source_refs.note: Topic 4.1.4 Queues (PDF 100-101, printed 97-98). Figure 4.3 (queue at a bank) is described in the text and shown in the original diagram.

blocks.text: A queue is like a line in front of the a bank or a ticket counter. The first person to get in line is the first person to be served. In a computer, a queue works the same way. It keeps track of things so that the first item added is the first one to be taken out. Just like in a bank line, you add things to the back and remove them from the front, following the FIFO (First-In, First-Out) principle, as shown in Figure 4.3.

blocks.alt: Black silhouettes of people standing in a line that gets smaller towards the back. An arrow labelled remove shows the first person leaving at the front, and a curved arrow shows a new person joining at the back.
blocks.caption: Figure 4.3: Queue of persons in front of the bank (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 4.3).
